reviewScope: Both functional-language references and ten actual language bodies: population aggregation and independently coin-filtered occurrence subsets.

questions.algorithm: Lambda-based continent filtering and population summation, using a fused conditional accumulate in C++ and the actual language pipeline elsewhere.
questions.review: Read pinned Java Country and QuestionA/QuestionB sources, then all five independently authored bodies. Provided Country objects expose actual getters; the private wire-tuple decoder is not passed to candidates. Exact continent contents, not country name or object identity, determine membership. Nonnegative populations and the 1000-by-million bound keep each actual int/Number sum exact. C# lazy Where/Sum, Java sequential filter/mapToInt/sum and Python lazy filter/map/sum do not materialize matching lists. C++ folds with a readonly capturing lambda over a const vector reference. JavaScript filter intentionally allocates matching references before reduce and its O(m) temporary storage is stated. Independent scalar-loop oracle covers exhaustive small occurrence lists, zero/no matches, duplicates, case/space distinctions, composed/decomposed accents, emoji and maximum billion total. Child observations check original array member identity/order and Country getter values; C++ supplied model fields and input reference are readonly. Five actual reordering variants retain the correct sum but fail mutation checks; five unfiltered-total variants fail result semantics. Neutral zero-return starters are executed and rejected, not credited from presence checks.

questions.algorithm: Evaluate one independent supplied fair coin per occurrence through the actual language filter/copy_if pipeline, materializing an ordered subset before returning.
questions.review: Read pinned Java QuestionA/QuestionB, then all five actual independently authored bodies. This is not fixed-cardinality sampling and is not merged with 17.3. Every occurrence has its own predicate call, even for equal integers; each occurrence subset has probability 2^-n, with original relative order retained. C#/Java/Python force lazy pipelines into concrete arrays/lists before releasing the borrowed coin source. JavaScript filter returns a fresh array; C++ copy_if writes a new vector through back_inserter and captures the source by reference. Empty input consumes no coins and returns an empty collection. Host grading accepts any valid observed ordered subset, never a fixed illustrated coin mapping. For n<=5, the private observer counts increasing match embeddings of the returned value subsequence and lifts it uniformly to compatible physical occurrence masks. A uniform lifted mask is equivalent to the desired aggregate observable law with duplicates. Independent exhaustive-mask Fraction tests execute the actual lifting helper and bound unresolved binary rejection prefixes. The established checker retains small unfinished decision mass as intervals and samples mask marginals/pairs/triples; large inputs receive readonly/subsequence, inclusion-frequency and size-moment checks. These finite checks are not claimed as a universal probability proof for arbitrary programs; the actual one-coin-per-occurrence reference proof covers all n. All five biased shared-coin, deduplicating and input-reordering implementations are compiled and rejected on two fixtures each. Five inverted-coin and five two-coin-XOR alternatives pass, including length-five duplicate cases whose valid longer decision trees exceed the exact exploration prefix. Maximum-length inputs, all-equal values, signed endpoints and concrete result types are executed.

languageBindingReview.csharp: Read Country[] binding and immutable private Country fields/getters. String operator == compares contents ordinally. Where plus selector Sum is lazy and uses a bounded int accumulator; array elements are snapshotted by reference identity before invocation. RandomSubset uses an injected FairCoinSource whose Next returns a boolean; native C++ borrows it by reference, while managed/dynamic languages use the supplied object. The concrete filter result is completed within the invocation, preserving source lifetime and original input order. Returned subset size is variable and repeated equal values remain separate coin decisions.
